title: WPMS/1173/2008 of DARSHAN SINGH Vs STATE AND OTHERS

paras.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
Writ Petition No. 1173 of 2008 (M/S)
Darshan Singh S/O Shri Uttam Singh, R/O Village Konti, Patti
Kemar, Tehsil Dhansali, District Tehri Garhwal
...... Petitioner.
Versus
State of Uttarakhand through District Magistrate, District Tehri
Garhwal and two others.
... Respondents.
Sri Ghanshyam Joshi, holding brief of Arvind Vashist, learned counsel for the
petitioner.
Sri K.P. Upadhyay, learned Additional C.S.C. for the respondents-State.
Date July 17, 2008.
Hon'ble B.S. Verma, J.
Sri Ghanshyam Joshi, holding brief of Sri Arvind
Vashist, learned counsel for the petitioner and Sri K.P. Upadhyay,
learned Additional Chief Standing Counsel for the State-respondents.
This writ petition has been filed for issue a writ
of mandamus commanding the respondents to construct Sentul-Patud
Gaon road without changing the survey conducted earlier by the
consent of public in general of the villages, who are beneficiary and
not to construct the road aforesaid according to new survey
allegedly made by the respondent nos. 2 and 3.
According to the petitioner Sentul-Patud Gaon road was
sanctioned by the respondent no. 1 and the road has already
been completed upto village Konti and now the remaining road has
to be constructed from village Konti to Patud Gaon and in
accordance with the alignment of the earlier survey, which was
duly approved by the Government.

The grievance of the petitioner is that earlier survey was
conducted with the consent of general public, but later-on, the
respondent no.2 conducted another survey by which the alignment
of the road had been changed and the road is being constructed on
the basis of second survey.
In the course of arguments, learned counsel for the
petitioner has submitted that the petitioner may be given liberty to
make a representation before the respondent no.3 and the
respondent no. 3 be directed to decide the representation of the
petitioner by a speaking order and the writ petition may be disposed
of finally today.
In the above facts and circumstances of the case,
liberty is given to the petitioner to make a representation before the
Superintending Engineer concerned-respondent no.3 within a
period of one week from today along with certified copy of this
order. If the representation is so made, the third respondent shall
consider the grievance of the petitioner and shall decide the
representation expeditiously by a reasoned order, preferably within
a period of four weeks thereafter.
With the above direction, the writ petition is disposed
of finally.
(B.S. Verma, J.)
RCP
